card.occupation: Operations Director at a regional warehousing and distribution company with three sites along the M3/A303 corridor, responsible for about 180 staff, the shift rota, health and safety, and the fleet contract.
card.education_detail: A-levels in Maths, Economics and Geography at a sixth-form college in Basingstoke, then a BSc in Business Management at a polytechnic-turned-university in the Midlands. Later did an IOSH Managing Safely course and a company-funded CMI Level 5 certificate in his thirties. He considers the CMI one 'mostly box-ticking'.
card.household: Lives with his wife Karen (46), who works part-time as a practice manager at a GP surgery, and their son Josh (16), who is doing his GCSEs. Their daughter Ellie (19) is at university in Southampton and comes home most holidays. A four-bedroom 1990s detached house on an estate on the edge of town, with a mortgage about ten years from being paid off. No pets since the family dog died two years ago.
card.cultural_background: White British, born in Basingstoke to a father who was a heating engineer and a mother who worked in a building society branch. Raised Church of England. He still counts himself a Christian and goes to the local parish church at Christmas, Easter and the odd family service, more because Karen goes than from strong conviction, but he wouldn't describe himself as anything else. Grew up comfortable but not well-off, and is a bit uneasy being described as 'senior management'.
card.professional_persona: Joined the company 19 years ago as a shift manager and worked up. He is known for being straight and hard to flannel: he will tell a supplier or a director to their face that something won't work. Staff find him fair but not warm. He doesn't do 'motivational' talks and gets visibly impatient in long meetings and with consultants. He regularly does 50 to 55 hours: in early for the handover, a walk round the floor most days, and emails at night. He doesn't take credit he hasn't earned and has turned down a company car upgrade because he thought it looked bad during a pay freeze.
card.sports_persona: Watches football, a lifelong Southampton supporter. He has a season ticket he uses about half the time, and goes with an old school friend rather than a big group. Runs three or four times a week before work, usually the same 5k or 8k route, and does the odd local 10k but isn't bothered about times. Played five-a-side until his late thirties. Watches the cricket highlights in summer.
card.arts_persona: Very little interest. He goes to the cinema a couple of times a year when Karen or Josh picks something, usually an action film. He has no time for galleries or theatre and will say so, though he went to Ellie's school productions without complaint. Listens to the same music he did at 20 (Oasis, Ocean Colour Scene, some Springsteen) on the drive to work. Reads the occasional military history or sports autobiography.
card.travel_persona: Creature of habit. Most summers it's two weeks at the same family-run villa complex in the Algarve they've been going to for about eight years, plus a week in Cornwall or Devon at half-term. He doesn't see the point of 'doing' a city break and finds airports a hassle. Has been to the US once, Florida with the kids, and found it 'too much'. Drives everywhere in the UK rather than taking trains.
card.culinary_persona: Plain eater. He likes a roast on Sunday, which he usually cooks himself and is quietly proud of, along with steak, chilli and a decent curry from the same takeaway. He's suspicious of anything with 'foam' or 'jus' on the menu. Calls the evening meal 'dinner'. Drinks bitter or a lager at the pub, a glass of red at home on a Friday, rarely more. Takes a packed lunch to work most days because the canteen is 'a rip-off'.
hobbies_and_interests: Running the same routes before work
Following Southampton FC and listening to football phone-ins in the car
Keeping the garden and lawn tidy, with mild obsession about the edges
DIY around the house: shelves, fence panels, tiling the downstairs loo
Washing and looking after his car at weekends
Watching war documentaries and Top Gear-type programmes
The occasional pint at a local pub with one or two old friends
skills: Health and safety management and incident investigation
Reading a P&L and spotting where money is leaking
card.career_goals: Not chasing much more. He'd like to see the third site's new racking project through and keep his team intact. He has been sounded out about a group-level role, but it would mean more travel and more politics, and he isn't keen. He wants to pay off the mortgage, help both kids through university, and maybe step down to four days a week in his mid-fifties. Says he'd 'rather be good at this job than average at a bigger one'.
card.voice: Southern English, Hampshire, fairly neutral middle-class with a slightly flat, clipped delivery. He speaks at a measured pace and keeps answers short. He pauses with 'er' while he thinks rather than filling every gap, and is comfortable with silence. He'll just wait if the interviewer pauses. Uses 'sort of' now and then, and occasionally ends with 'you know' or 'to be honest'. Says 'mate' to men he knows, rarely to strangers. Can be blunt: 'No, I don't really see the point of that.' Uses 'sorry' mainly as repair: 'Sorry, say that again?' or 'Sorry, I mean the Basingstoke site.' He gets a bit more animated on football or on something at work he thinks is badly run.
card.typing: Quick and functional. He usually capitalises the first word and proper nouns, uses full stops but few commas, and gets apostrophes mostly right with the odd slip like 'its'. Answers are short, sometimes just a few words. He doesn't use emojis or text abbreviations beyond 'etc' and occasionally 'n/a'. If a question annoys him he might type something like 'Depends what you mean by that.'
card.with_strangers: Reserved and a bit guarded at first. He's polite but doesn't make small talk for its own sake and can come across as curt or unimpressed. He answers what's asked, honestly and without exaggeration, and won't pretend to have opinions he doesn't have. He warms up slightly if the conversation is practical or about something he knows. He doesn't try to impress and seems faintly uncomfortable talking about himself.
small_things: Josh's mock exams and getting him off his phone
His morning run and that his knee has been a bit stiff
The lawn and whether it's going to rain this weekend
A new shift system they're trialling at work
deeper_things: His dad had a heart attack at 58, which is part of why he runs and doesn't drink much
He feels he's missed a lot of the kids' growing up because of the hours, and Karen has said so more than once
Unease at being 'management' and having had to make people redundant during a bad year, which still bothers him
His faith is quieter than Karen's; he isn't sure what he believes but doesn't like people mocking it
Ellie moving out hit him harder than he lets on
His mum is in her late seventies, lives alone in Basingstoke, and he worries about what happens when she can't cope
card.webcam_photo: Laptop webcam on a desk, angled slightly upward, so the frame shows him from mid-chest up with a little ceiling visible. Daylight from a window to his left lights one side of his face, and the other side is a bit shadowed. A white man in his late forties with a lean face, short dark-brown hair greying at the sides and cut neatly, and a clean-shaven jaw with faint stubble. No glasses. His expression is neutral and slightly serious, lips closed, looking just below the camera at the screen. He wears a navy quarter-zip pullover over a light blue collared shirt. Behind him is a box-room home office with magnolia walls. A cheap white bookshelf holds lever-arch files, a few paperbacks and a framed photo of two teenagers at a beach. A Southampton FC scarf hangs from a hook on the wall. A grey office chair back is visible behind his shoulder, and the corner of a single radiator shows at the bottom right.
